Must export a default async function: `export default async (ctx) => { ... }`. ctx.args holds the input parameters (declare them via `parameters` in `body`); ctx.config holds plain string variables mapped into the tool's execution_context. ctx.secrets and ctx.auth_connections are write-only credential references: a secret can only be interpolated into a fetch request header (e.g. `Authorization: Bearer ${ctx.secrets.MY_KEY}`) and an auth connection only into the `X-With-Auth-Connection` header; neither can be read or logged. description.text: Create a procedure on an agent branch. A procedure is a standard operating procedure the agent follows for one specific task: trigger says when the agent should use it, content says what to do. There are two types. A free-form procedure (type=free_form) is markdown instructions that are injected into the prompt when the procedure is active; the agent reads them and uses judgment about wording and order. A structured procedure (type=deterministic) is a list of typed steps the agent runs in a fixed order, every time. Set trigger as the top-level field; never write it inside content. For structured content, send the steps object JSON-encoded in content; its shape and rules are documented at https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/procedures/structured-procedures. Do not connect workflow edges to a structured procedure: those connections are removed when the platform rebuilds its execution form. Chain structured procedures with a Sub-procedure step; entry from a matching trigger and completion are platform-managed. The procedure is a draft until the agent is published; saving the draft (agents_create_draft) and publishing both validate structured procedures and return per-procedure errors with the path of each offending step.

tool_error_handling_mode.description: Controls how tool errors are processed before being shared with the agent. enable_client_message.title: Enable Client Message

custom_sip_headers.description: Custom SIP headers to include when transferring the call. Each header can be either a static value or a dynamic variable reference.

sip_refer_play_dialtone.title: Sip Refer Play Dialtone
sip_refer_play_dialtone.description: When True, a ringing tone is played on the original call leg while a SIP REFER transfer completes. The tone is carried over RTP to the SIP peer executing the REFER, so disable this if the receiving system (e.g. an SBC or contact center) should not hear it. When disabled the caller hears silence until the transfer completes. SIP REFER transfers only.

UUITransferConfig.title: UUITransferConfig
UUITransferConfig.description:
User-to-User Information envelope for SIP REFER transfers (RFC 7433).

Outbound payloads are hex-encoded (the only encoding RFC 7433 defines). The
protocol discriminator axis lets per-platform formats (Talkdesk, Genesys, ...)
be expressed by configuration rather than scattered transfer flags. Further
axes (ASCII encoding, header name, purpose/content parameters) can be added
here without touching the transfer model.

SkipTurnToolConfig.title: SkipTurnToolConfig
SkipTurnToolConfig.description:
Allows the agent to explicitly skip its turn.

This tool should be invoked by the LLM when the user indicates they would like
to think or take a short pause before continuing the conversation—e.g. when
they say: "Give me a second", "Let me think", or "One moment please".  After
calling this tool, the assistant should not speak until the user speaks
again, or if wait_timeout_secs is set, until that wait elapses and the
agent generates a check-in.

use_out_of_band_dtmf.title: Use Out Of Band Dtmf
use_out_of_band_dtmf.description: Send DTMF tones as out-of-band RTP events (RFC 4733) instead of in-band audio. Only effective for SIP trunk imported numbers.

suppress_turn_after_dtmf.title: Suppress Turn After Dtmf
suppress_turn_after_dtmf.description: If true, the agent will not generate further speech after playing DTMF tones. This prevents the agent's speech from interfering with IVR systems.

PlayDTMFToolConfig.title: PlayDTMFToolConfig
PlayDTMFToolConfig.description:
Allows the agent to play DTMF tones during a phone call.

This tool can be used to interact with automated phone systems, such as
navigating phone menus, entering extensions, or inputting numeric codes.

voicemail_message.title: Voicemail Message
voicemail_message.description: Optional message to leave on voicemail when detected. If not provided, the call will end immediately when voicemail is detected. Supports dynamic variables (e.g., {{system__time}}, {{system__call_duration_secs}}, {{custom_variable}}).

VoicemailDetectionToolConfig.title: VoicemailDetectionToolConfig
VoicemailDetectionToolConfig.description:
Allows the agent to detect when a voicemail system is encountered.

This tool should be invoked by the LLM when it detects that the call has been
answered by a voicemail system rather than a human. If a voicemail message
is configured, it will be played; otherwise the call will end immediately.

Pass an empty new_string to delete the passage. Returns the field's new content. agent_md and user_md save at once. system_prompt and first_message are staged in the caller's draft of branch_id (branch_id is required for them) and are not live until that draft is published in the agent editor; the result's staged field says which happened. workspace.md can't be edited here. For the agent's main branch, pass the first branch returned by agents_list_branches. Follow up with agents_get_version for one version's metadata, or agents_get with version_id for the full configuration at that version; to see what a version changed, compare its configuration with its in_branch_parent_id's.

A production agent's full configuration can run to hundreds of KB, so start here and only call agents_get, scoped with fields, for a value this summary does not carry. A procedure's trigger says when it fires, not everything its body handles: before concluding no procedure covers a case, use agents_search_procedures and read the candidates with agents_get_procedure_draft.

description.text: Query an ElevenLabs Agent's analytics: time-bucketed rows over a window of up to 90 days, optionally grouped by up to two columns and filtered. This is the tool for measuring change (volume, duration, cost, success, ratings, latency, tool calls) and for comparing cohorts, such as this week against last: run the same query for both windows and compare. metric conversations returns cnt, duration (sum, seconds), cost (sum, credits), llm_cost, avg_rating and rating_count; latency, tools and rating return their own metric columns, so read the returned columns. Columns differ by metric. conversations and rating group and filter by success, branch_id, language, status, direction, rating, feedback_type, transfer_to_number, voicemail_detection, data_collection_<field id>, evaluation_criteria_<criterion id> and dynamic_variable_<name>; agents_get_config_summary lists the agent's criterion and field ids. tools groups by tool_id, tool_type or tool_name; latency by branch_id, event_name, llm_model, rag_embedding_model or tts_model. Both filter on event columns such as branch_id, version_id, language, llm_model, tts_model or tool_type. Topics are not a column: use agents_get_topics_summary for per-topic numbers. Data can lag live conversations by a few minutes.

description.text: Search the text of conversation transcripts and return the matching messages, each with its conversation_id, transcript_index, message text, and relevance score. This is the only way to find conversations by something that was said; agents_list_conversations filters on structured attributes and cannot search transcript text. Wrap text_query in double quotes to match the terms as written (do this for error codes, identifiers, and anything a user pasted); leave it unquoted to match fuzzily, tolerating one character of difference per term. Neither form is a substring or phrase match -- a multi-word query matches messages containing all of the terms in any position -- so read the returned text before treating a hit as an occurrence. Results are messages, not conversations: deduplicate by conversation_id before counting.

description.description: Explains to the calling LLM what this tool does and when to use it.

source_code.description: JavaScript/TypeScript source. Must export a default async function: `export default async (ctx) => { ... }`. ctx.args holds the input parameters (declare them via `parameters` in `body`); ctx.config holds plain string variables mapped into the tool's execution_context. ctx.secrets and ctx.auth_connections are write-only credential references: a secret can only be interpolated into a fetch request header (e.g. `Authorization: Bearer ${ctx.secrets.MY_KEY}`) and an auth connection only into the `X-With-Auth-Connection` header; neither can be read or logged. There is no ctx.env, and npm dependencies are not supported: only the sandbox runtime's built-ins (e.g. fetch) are available.

response_timeout_secs.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the code to finish executing. 1-30, default 20.

body.description: Advanced compatibility escape hatch: the full raw request body sent to the underlying tools API (e.g. to set `parameters`, `execution_context`, `dynamic_variables`, or `response_mocks`). Overrides the compact fields above when present.

description.text: Update a code tool. Requires an Enterprise workspace plan. Docs: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/tools/code-tools

The guardrail always gets a single <conversation_history> transcript ending in the evaluated reply, marked 'AGENT [current reply]:'. 0 (default) adds no prior history (just that line); 1 adds the latest user message onward. Defaults to 0 when never set.

history_include_tool_calls.title: History Include Tool Calls
history_include_tool_calls.description: When enabled, the history also renders the agent's tool calls, their input arguments, and the tool results, interleaved with the text, so an action between two agent messages is visible. Off by default: history shows only user and agent text. Tool payloads can be large and can mislead smaller evaluator models, so enabling this raises token cost. Defaults to false when never set.

evaluate_full_response_only.title: Evaluate Full Response Only
evaluate_full_response_only.description: Evaluate once against the complete non-TTS response instead of cumulative partials. Requires blocking mode. Defaults to false when never set.

LLMServiceTier.description:

STANDARD: default price and throughput.
FAST: pays a per-token price premium for higher throughput / lower latency.
    See OpenAI's fast mode: https://openai.com/api-fast-mode/ and, for Gemini, Vertex
    Priority PayGo: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/priority-paygo. Defaults to "standard" when never set.

description.text: Update the draft of a procedure on an agent branch. Send name, content, type and trigger in full. type must be the procedure's existing type: a procedure's type cannot be changed after creation, so to convert between free_form and deterministic, create a new procedure instead. For structured content, send the steps object JSON-encoded in content; its shape and rules are documented at https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/procedures/structured-procedures. Do not connect workflow edges to a structured procedure: those connections are removed when the platform rebuilds its execution form. Chain structured procedures with a Sub-procedure step; entry from a matching trigger and completion are platform-managed. The change is a draft until the agent is published; saving the draft (agents_create_draft) and publishing both validate structured procedures and return per-procedure errors.

No llm nodes.

description.text: Set which agents an ElevenLabs Agent can run as sub-agents. A sub-agent answers one self-contained request through the agent's run_subagent tool and its reply comes back to the calling agent, which keeps the conversation: it is not a transfer (that is agents_update_transfer_to_agent_tool), and the sub-agent never sees the transcript. It runs server-side with no client attached, so it can only use server-side tools; a client tool call waits out its timeout. agents replaces the whole list, so read the agent's current conversation_config.agent.subagent_config first and send every sub-agent you want to keep, or [] to remove them all. self_subagent lets the agent run a fresh copy of itself; send null to turn it off. Fails with subagents_not_available when the workspace doesn't have sub-agents yet, with subagents_not_allowed_in_zrm for zero retention or encrypted agents, and when the agent has the legacy Run Subagent built-in tool. Each target must be an Agents Platform agent in the same workspace that you can run. Returns agent_id, branch_id and version_id, and under config, keyed by path, the stored values of conversation_config.agent.subagent_config.agents, conversation_config.agent.subagent_config.self_subagent as saved by this call, limited to the fields this tool accepts.

The tone is carried over RTP to the SIP peer executing the REFER, so disable this if the receiving system (e.g. an SBC or contact center) should not hear it. When disabled the caller hears silence until the transfer completes. SIP REFER transfers only.

protocol discriminator axis lets per-platform formats (Talkdesk, Genesys, ...)
be expressed by configuration rather than scattered transfer flags. Further
axes (ASCII encoding, header name, purpose/content parameters) can be added
here without touching the transfer model.

wait_timeout_secs.title: Wait Timeout Secs
wait_timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait after skip_turn before the agent generates a contextual check-in. The "End conversation after silence" timer is paused during the wait. -1 disables the wait: after skip_turn the agent stays silent until the caller speaks, and that timer keeps running. Applies to voice conversations only.

SkipTurnToolConfig.title: SkipTurnToolConfig
SkipTurnToolConfig.description:
Allows the agent to explicitly skip its turn.

This tool should be invoked by the LLM when the user indicates they would like
to think or take a short pause before continuing the conversation—e.g. when
they say: "Give me a second", "Let me think", or "One moment please".  After
calling this tool, the assistant should not speak until the user speaks
again, or if wait_timeout_secs is set, until that wait elapses and the
agent generates a check-in.

use_out_of_band_dtmf.title: Use Out Of Band Dtmf
use_out_of_band_dtmf.description: Send DTMF tones as out-of-band RTP events (RFC 4733) instead of in-band audio. Only effective for SIP trunk imported numbers.

suppress_turn_after_dtmf.title: Suppress Turn After Dtmf
suppress_turn_after_dtmf.description: If true, the agent will not generate further speech after playing DTMF tones. This prevents the agent's speech from interfering with IVR systems.

PlayDTMFToolConfig.title: PlayDTMFToolConfig
PlayDTMFToolConfig.description:
Allows the agent to play DTMF tones during a phone call.

This tool can be used to interact with automated phone systems, such as
navigating phone menus, entering extensions, or inputting numeric codes.

voicemail_message.title: Voicemail Message
voicemail_message.description: Optional message to leave on voicemail when detected. If not provided, the call will end immediately when voicemail is detected. Supports dynamic variables (e.g., {{system__time}}, {{system__call_duration_secs}}, {{custom_variable}}).

VoicemailDetectionToolConfig.title: VoicemailDetectionToolConfig
VoicemailDetectionToolConfig.description:
Allows the agent to detect when a voicemail system is encountered.

This tool should be invoked by the LLM when it detects that the call has been
answered by a voicemail system rather than a human. If a voicemail message
is configured, it will be played; otherwise the call will end immediately.

disable_interruptions.description: DEPRECATED: use `interruption_mode` instead. If true, the user will not be able to interrupt the agent while this tool is running.

'allow' (default) lets the user interrupt at any time, 'disable_during_tool' suppresses interruptions only while the tool is running, 'disable_during_tool_and_turn' suppresses interruptions while the tool runs and for the agent response that follows it.

turn_timeout.title: Turn Timeout
turn_timeout.description: Maximum wait time for the user's reply before re-engaging the user. Defaults to 7.0 when never set.

initial_wait_time.title: Initial Wait Time
initial_wait_time.description: How long the agent will wait for the user to start the conversation if the first message is empty. If not set, uses the regular turn_timeout.

silence_end_call_timeout.title: Silence End Call Timeout
silence_end_call_timeout.description: Maximum wait time since the user last spoke before terminating the call. Defaults to -1 when never set.

mode.description: The mode of turn detection. Defaults to "turn" when never set.

turn_eagerness.description: Controls how eager the agent is to respond. Low = less eager (waits longer), Standard = default eagerness, High = more eager (responds sooner). Defaults to "normal" when never set.

spelling_patience.description: Controls if the agent should be more patient when user is spelling numbers and named entities. Auto = model based, Off = never wait extra. Defaults to "auto" when never set.

speculative_turn.title: Speculative Turn
speculative_turn.description: When enabled, starts generating LLM responses during silence before full turn confidence is reached, reducing perceived latency. May increase LLM costs. Defaults to false when never set.

retranscribe_on_turn_timeout.title: Retranscribe On Turn Timeout
retranscribe_on_turn_timeout.description: When enabled, if VAD detects no speech, attempts to re-transcribe accumulated audio at turn timeout. Disables silence discount billing while enabled for the active agent or workflow node. Defaults to false when never set.

interruption_ignore_terms.title: Interruption Ignore Terms
interruption_ignore_terms.description: List of terms that should not trigger an interruption when spoken by the user (e.g. 'gotcha', 'understood'). Uses case-insensitive exact matching.

interruption_ignore_term_languages.title: Interruption Ignore Term Languages
interruption_ignore_term_languages.description: Language codes for which preset ignore-term categories have been activated. Stored explicitly so display is not inferred from term overlap.

merge_with_default_ignore_terms.title: Merge With Default Ignore Terms
merge_with_default_ignore_terms.description: When enabled, the curated default terms for interruption_ignore_term_languages are used in addition to interruption_ignore_terms. Defaults to false when never set.

transcribe_on_disabled_interruptions.title: Transcribe On Disabled Interruptions
transcribe_on_disabled_interruptions.description: When interruptions are disabled, still transcribe what the user says so it can carry into the next turn. When off, user speech during a non-interruptible turn is ignored and won't trigger a turn. Defaults to false when never set.

soft_timeout_config.description: Configuration for soft timeout functionality. Provides immediate feedback during longer LLM responses.

noisy_environment_detection.title: Noisy Environment Detection
noisy_environment_detection.description: When enabled, the agent politely suggests the user move somewhere quieter when it hears other voices in the background. This improves transcription and turn-taking accuracy. Defaults to false when never set.

noisy_environment_message.title: Noisy Environment Message
noisy_environment_message.description: What the agent says when it detects a noisy environment. Defaults to "Uhh ... sorry, I'm picking up some noise in the background. Could you move somewhere quieter?" when never set.

return_full_agent.description: Return the whole agent document instead of only what this tool writes. For debugging; it is large.

TurnEagerness.title: TurnEagerness
TurnEagerness.description: Agent's eagerness to respond. Higher values make agent wait for higher turn probability. Defaults to "normal" when never set.

SpellingPatience.title: SpellingPatience
SpellingPatience.description: Controls if the agent should be more patient when user is spelling numbers and named entities. Defaults to "auto" when never set.

TurnModel.title: TurnModel
TurnModel.description: Version of the turn detection model to use. Defaults to "turn_v3" when never set.

timeout_seconds.title: Timeout Seconds
timeout_seconds.description: Time in seconds before showing the predefined message while waiting for LLM response. Set to -1 to disable. Defaults to -1.0 when never set.

message.title: Message
message.description: Message to show when the first soft timeout is reached while waiting for LLM response. Supports dynamic variables (e.g., {{system__time}}, {{custom_variable}}). Defaults to "Hhmmmm...yeah." when never set.

additional_soft_timeout_messages.title: Additional Soft Timeout Messages
additional_soft_timeout_messages.description: Extra static filler messages for subsequent soft timeouts in the same LLM generation. The first timeout uses `message`. If fewer messages are configured than `max_soft_timeouts_per_generation`, the last configured message is repeated; otherwise a built-in filler is used.

use_llm_generated_message.title: Use Llm Generated Message
use_llm_generated_message.description: If enabled, the soft timeout message will be generated dynamically instead of using the static message. Defaults to false when never set.

randomize_fillers.title: Randomize Fillers
randomize_fillers.description: If enabled, shuffle the order of static soft timeout messages once at the start of each turn. Only applies when use_llm_generated_message is false. Defaults to false when never set.

max_soft_timeouts_per_generation.title: Max Soft Timeouts Per Generation
max_soft_timeouts_per_generation.description: Maximum filler messages while waiting for a single LLM response. Fires every timeout_seconds until the LLM streams content or this limit is reached. Defaults to 1 when never set.

llm_generated_message_prompt_override.title: Llm Generated Message Prompt Override
llm_generated_message_prompt_override.description: Custom prompt for generating the soft timeout filler message when use_llm_generated_message is enabled. Recent conversation context is provided as a separate user message. If not set, the default prompt will be used. Supports dynamic variables (e.g., {{system__time}}, {{custom_variable}}).
examples: Output a SHORT neutral filler phrase (1-4 words MAX) acknowledging you heard the user.

disable_until_first_user_message.title: Disable Until First User Message
disable_until_first_user_message.description: When true, soft timeout fillers are suppressed until the conversation has at least one real user message. Prevents fillers during the agent's opening turn (e.g. workflow generate-immediately / tool calls before the user speaks). Defaults to false when never set.

SoftTimeoutConfig.title: SoftTimeoutConfig
SoftTimeoutConfig.description: Configuration for soft timeout functionality during LLM response generation.

description.text: Set how an ElevenLabs Agent decides when to speak: turn timeouts, silence and end-call thresholds, the turn detection mode and eagerness, backchannelling, and how it handles a caller who says nothing. voice_id.description: The voice ID to use for TTS. Defaults to "cjVigY5qzO86Huf0OWal" when never set.

supported_voices.title: Supported Voices
supported_voices.description: Additional supported voices for the agent

expressive_mode.title: Expressive Mode
expressive_mode.description: When enabled, applies expressive audio tags prompt. Automatically disabled for non-v3 models. Defaults to true when never set.

suggested_audio_tags.title: Suggested Audio Tags
suggested_audio_tags.description: Suggested audio tags to boost expressive speech (for eleven_v3 and eleven_v3_conversational models). The agent can still use other tags not listed here.

agent_output_audio_format.description: The audio format to use for TTS. Defaults to "pcm_16000" when never set.

optimize_streaming_latency.description: Deprecated: this field is a no-op and is ignored. Defaults to 3 when never set.

stability.title: Stability
stability.description: The stability of generated speech. Defaults to 0.5 when never set.

speed.title: Speed
speed.description: The speed of generated speech. Defaults to 1.0 when never set.

similarity_boost.title: Similarity Boost
similarity_boost.description: The similarity boost for generated speech. Defaults to 0.8 when never set.

clone_strength.title: Clone Strength
clone_strength.description: The clone strength for generated speech. Defaults to 0.0 when never set.

text_normalisation_type.description: Method for converting numbers to words before converting text to speech. If set to SYSTEM_PROMPT, the system prompt will be updated to include normalization instructions. If set to ELEVENLABS, the text will be normalized after generation, incurring slight additional latency. Defaults to "system_prompt" when never set.

enable_phoneme_tags.title: Enable Phoneme Tags
enable_phoneme_tags.description: Opt-in to SSML phoneme tag handling for V3 models. When enabled, phoneme tags (inline and from pronunciation dictionaries) are parsed into inline IPA before being sent to the model. Defaults to true when never set.

audio_effects.description: Optional TTS effects spec: filter preset, distance (proximity EQ), and environment (convolution reverb).

return_full_agent.description: Return the whole agent document instead of only what this tool writes. For debugging; it is large.

tag.title: Tag
tag.description: Audio tag to use (for best performance, 1-2 words, e.g., 'happy', 'excited')

description.title: Description
description.description: Optional description of when to use this tag

TextNormalisationType.title: TextNormalisationType
TextNormalisationType.description: Method for converting numbers to words before sending to TTS. Defaults to "system_prompt" when never set.

pronunciation_dictionary_id.title: Pronunciation Dictionary Id
pronunciation_dictionary_id.description: The ID of the pronunciation dictionary

version_id.title: Version Id
version_id.description: The ID of the version of the pronunciation dictionary

PydanticPronunciationDictionaryVersionLo.title: PydanticPronunciationDictionaryVersionLocator
PydanticPronunciationDictionaryVersionLo.description:
A locator for other documents to be able to reference a specific dictionary and it's version.
This is a pydantic version of PronunciationDictionaryVersionLocatorDBModel.
Required to ensure compat with the rest of the agent data models.

filter_preset_id.title: Filter Preset Id
filter_preset_id.description: ID of a filter preset that colors the voice, such as `phone` or `old_radio`. List valid IDs with `GET /v1/audio-effects/catalog`.

distance.title: Distance
distance.description: How far the speaker sounds from the microphone, from 0 (close, unchanged) to 1 (far). Higher values roll off low and high frequencies and, when an environment is set, shift the balance from the dry voice toward the reverb. Defaults to 0.0 when never set.

environment_id.title: Environment Id
environment_id.description: ID of a reverb environment that places the voice in a space, such as `small_room` or `hall`. List valid IDs with `GET /v1/audio-effects/catalog`. Reverb is rendered in stereo and adds a tail of up to several seconds after the speech ends.

background_noise_id.title: Background Noise Id
background_noise_id.description: ID of a background noise bed looped under the voice, such as `cafe` or `keyboard`. List valid IDs with `GET /v1/audio-effects/catalog`.

send_level.title: Send Level
send_level.description: How much of the voice feeds the reverb, from 0 (none) to 1 (full). Only applies when `environment_id` is set; 0 turns the reverb off. Defaults to 1.0 when never set.

pan.title: Pan
pan.description: Stereo position of the voice, from -1 (hard left) through 0 (center) to 1 (hard right). Only the voice is panned; reverb and background noise stay centered. Defaults to 0.0 when never set.

EffectsSpec-Input.title: EffectsSpec
EffectsSpec-Input.description:
Audio effects applied to generated speech: a filter preset, perceived distance, a reverb
environment, a background noise bed, and stereo panning. Leave every field at its default
to get unprocessed audio.

description.description: Description of when the tool should be used and what it does. Leave empty to use the default description that's optimized for the specific tool type. Defaults to "" when never set.

response_timeout_secs.title: Response Timeout Secs
response_timeout_secs.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the tool call to complete. Defaults to 20 when never set.

disable_interruptions.title: Disable Interruptions
disable_interruptions.description: DEPRECATED: use `interruption_mode` instead. If true, the user will not be able to interrupt the agent while this tool is running. Defaults to false when never set.

interruption_mode.description: Controls whether the user can interrupt the agent around this tool call. 'allow' (default) lets the user interrupt at any time, 'disable_during_tool' suppresses interruptions only while the tool is running, 'disable_during_tool_and_turn' suppresses interruptions while the tool runs and for the agent response that follows it. Defaults to "allow" when never set.

force_pre_tool_speech.title: Force Pre Tool Speech
force_pre_tool_speech.description: DEPRECATED: use `pre_tool_speech` instead. If true, the agent will speak before the tool call. Defaults to false when never set.

pre_tool_speech.description: Controls whether the agent speaks before this tool is called. 'auto' (default) decides based on recent tool latency, 'force' always asks the agent to speak, 'off' fully opts out regardless of latency. Defaults to "auto" when never set.

assignments.title: Assignments
assignments.description: Configuration for extracting values from tool responses and assigning them to dynamic variables

tool_call_sound.description: Predefined tool call sound type to play during tool execution. If not specified, no tool call sound will be played.

tool_call_sound_behavior.description: Determines when the tool call sound should play. 'auto' only plays when there's pre-tool speech, 'always' plays for every tool call. Defaults to "auto" when never set.

tool_error_handling_mode.description: Controls how tool errors are processed before being shared with the agent. 'auto' determines handling based on tool type (summarized for native integrations, hide for others), 'summarized' sends an LLM-generated summary, 'passthrough' sends the raw error, 'hide' does not share the error with the agent. Defaults to "auto" when never set.

return_full_agent.description: Return the whole agent document instead of only what this tool writes. For debugging; it is large.

source.title: Source
source.description: The source to extract the value from. Currently only 'response' is supported. Defaults to "response" when never set.

dynamic_variable.title: Dynamic Variable
dynamic_variable.description: The name of the dynamic variable to assign the extracted value to

value_path.title: Value Path
value_path.description: Dot notation path to extract the value from the source (e.g., 'user.name' or 'data.0.id')

sanitize.title: Sanitize
sanitize.description: If true, this assignment's value will be removed from the tool response before sending to the LLM and transcript, but still processed for variable assignment. Defaults to false when never set.

preserve_native_type.title: Preserve Native Type
preserve_native_type.description: If true, non-scalar values (lists, objects) extracted from the tool response are stored as their native type instead of being stringified to JSON. Enable this to use extracted arrays directly as list dynamic variables. Defaults to false when never set.

DynamicVariableAssignment.title: DynamicVariableAssignment
DynamicVariableAssignment.description: Configuration for extracting values from tool responses and assigning them to dynamic variables.

ToolCallSoundType.title: ToolCallSoundType
ToolCallSoundType.description: Predefined tool call sounds; ``None`` means no sound.

ToolCallSoundBehavior.title: ToolCallSoundBehavior
ToolCallSoundBehavior.description: Determines how the tool call sound should be played. Defaults to "auto" when never set.

ToolErrorHandlingMode.title: ToolErrorHandlingMode
ToolErrorHandlingMode.description: Controls how tool errors are processed before being shared with the agent. Defaults to "auto" when never set.

voicemail_message.title: Voicemail Message
voicemail_message.description: Optional message to leave on voicemail when detected. If not provided, the call will end immediately when voicemail is detected. Supports dynamic variables (e.g., {{system__time}}, {{system__call_duration_secs}}, {{custom_variable}}).

VoicemailDetectionToolConfig.title: VoicemailDetectionToolConfig
VoicemailDetectionToolConfig.description:
Allows the agent to detect when a voicemail system is encountered.

This tool should be invoked by the LLM when it detects that the call has been
answered by a voicemail system rather than a human. If a voicemail message
is configured, it will be played; otherwise the call will end immediately.

description.text: Replace the whole conversation workflow graph of an ElevenLabs Agent. This tool takes the graph as an opaque object and does not describe its shape, so it is only usable when you already have a complete workflow document to send; building one from scratch is not something this tool can guide. description.text: Put an existing asset or a previous generation on the flow as a node, so it can be wired into another node's reference input with creative_connect_flow_nodes. Reference inputs (reference_images, start_frame, image, audio, and similar) are input ports wired with edges, never model_parameters. The returned node id is authoritative — some calls return an already-existing node rather than creating one.

flow_id.description: The flow to act on, as returned by creative_create_flow or creative_generate_in_flow. Omit it for a one-off generation and a new flow is created. Always pass it when this generation will be combined with another: nodes on different flows cannot be connected, so allocate one with creative_create_flow up front and reuse it.

node_type.description: The type of node to create.

prompt.description: The node's prompt, as plain text.

model_id.description: The model to generate with. Pick one that suits node_type. Go looking for a different one when the request implies something the default may not do — a specific resolution or aspect, rendered text, a long duration, a named style or a named provider. creative_get_flow_node_types lists what this workspace can actually run; creative_get_model_guide explains how to prompt one. Pick by what the request needs: gpt-image-2 for rendered text, infographics, UI mockups or multi-panel layouts, and it takes up to 10 reference images; gemini-3-pro-image for editing an existing image, composing several into one, or holding a character consistent across shots; bytedance-seedream-5.5 for multi-round edits that keep the rest of the image intact, transparent backgrounds, and small or multilingual text, up to 4K UHD; bytedance-seedream-5-pro for photorealism, product shots, multilingual text and dense infographics, but caps at 2K; bytedance-seedream-5-lite for the same strengths as 5-pro when up to 3K is needed; flux-3-image for native 2K/4K, the strongest text rendering and layout control in the FLUX family, and edits and composes up to 10 references; krea-3 for aesthetic, art-directed looks at up to 2K, and edits and composes up to 8 references; flux-2-pro for fine detail and strict prompt adherence, and the FLUX variant to pick when two or more reference images must be combined (up to 5); flux-1-kontext for a single reference image only — do not pick it to combine two or more; bytedance-omnihuman-v1.5 for animating a static image into a lip-synced talking-head video with an audio track, not dubbing existing video; creatify-aurora for turning a single image and an audio clip into a studio-grade talking-head video, not editing existing video; sync-lipsync-v3 for dubbing existing video with new audio, not animating a still image; sync-lipsync-v2-pro for dubbing existing video with new audio, the same use as sync-lipsync-v3, not animating a still image; veed-lipsync for editing or lip-syncing existing video within ElevenCreative workflows, not animating a still image. Others exist; see creative_get_model_guide.

description.text:
Use this when the file the user wants as a reference is already reachable — attached to this conversation, or at a direct https URL they gave you. We fetch it and store it as an asset, so nothing has to be uploaded again. Pass flow_id to place it on that flow as a reference node in the same call — its modality (image/video/audio) is derived from the file itself — then pass the returned node_id as connect_from to a generation tool. description.text: Copy nodes on a flow without running them or touching the originals. Each copy keeps its model, parameters, prompt and asset, is placed offset from its original, and by default is wired to the same sources (copy_incoming_edges); connections between two copied nodes link the copies to each other. Pass labels to name the copies. Returns duplicated, a map of original node_id to copy node_id, plus node_urls for the copies. This never starts a generation.

connect_from.description: Existing node IDs that should feed INTO this new node. Pass these when you already know the upstream wiring — the canvas places the new node correctly on creation instead of parking it first and reflowing later. This is how a reference node created by creative_upload_flow_reference (or creative_add_flow_asset_node) gets wired into this generation — the node must already exist on this same flow_id. A node_id only ever comes from a tool result, creative_upload_flow_reference's widget context, or creative_get_flow — never from memory or invention. If you do not have one yet, call creative_get_flow and read it from there rather than guessing a name like 'reference'. For an image edit driven by a reference — 'change X into Y in this image' — use gpt-image-2.5-sunburst unless the user names a model. It is the default for this specifically; the plain text-to-image default does not apply once a reference is wired.

flow_id.description: The flow to act on, as returned by creative_create_flow or creative_generate_in_flow. Omit it for a one-off generation and a new flow is created. Always pass it when this generation will be combined with another: nodes on different flows cannot be connected, so allocate one with creative_create_flow up front and reuse it.

model_id.description: The model to generate with. Use gpt-image-2.5-sunburst unless the user asks for something specific. Go looking for a different one when the request implies something the default may not do — a specific resolution or aspect, rendered text, a long duration, a named style or a named provider. creative_get_flow_node_types lists what this workspace can actually run; creative_get_model_guide explains how to prompt one. Pick by what the request needs: gpt-image-2 for rendered text, infographics, UI mockups or multi-panel layouts, and it takes up to 10 reference images; gemini-3-pro-image for editing an existing image, composing several into one, or holding a character consistent across shots; bytedance-seedream-5.5 for multi-round edits that keep the rest of the image intact, transparent backgrounds, and small or multilingual text, up to 4K UHD; bytedance-seedream-5-pro for photorealism, product shots, multilingual text and dense infographics, but caps at 2K; bytedance-seedream-5-lite for the same strengths as 5-pro when up to 3K is needed; flux-3-image for native 2K/4K, the strongest text rendering and layout control in the FLUX family, and edits and composes up to 10 references; krea-3 for aesthetic, art-directed looks at up to 2K, and edits and composes up to 8 references; flux-2-pro for fine detail and strict prompt adherence, and the FLUX variant to pick when two or more reference images must be combined (up to 5); flux-1-kontext for a single reference image only — do not pick it to combine two or more.

description.text:
Edit an existing image already on this flow: pass its node_id as connect_from and it starts at once. That node can be one an earlier creative_generate_image call on this same flow just produced ("make it darker", "same image but at sunset"), one from creative_add_flow_asset_node, or one from creative_upload_flow_reference. It must be on this flow_id — pass back the flow_id the earlier call returned rather than letting a new flow be created; nodes on different flows cannot be connected. connect_from is required; a call with none raises — call creative_upload_flow_reference first for a file on the user's own machine. Never say this connector cannot edit images, and never ask the user to attach a file to the chat.
Returns flow_id, node_id and session_ids, plus a url to keep editing on the canvas. If a view renders it tracks progress on its own; otherwise poll creative_get_flow_run_status until all_completed or has_failures is true.
Spends credits: never call this a second time to retry.
For an image edit driven by a reference — 'change X into Y in this image' — use gpt-image-2.5-sunburst unless the user names a model. It is the default for this specifically; the plain text-to-image default does not apply once a reference is wired.

description.text: Run a bash command in an isolated, offline sandbox with ffmpeg, ffprobe, mediainfo, vips and python3 (numpy, pillow, librosa, pyloudnorm, soundfile, pysubs2). Use it for edits no node does: trimming, concatenating, re-encoding, mixing audio, measuring loudness, burning subtitles, batch image work. Pass flow node IDs, generation IDs or library asset IDs in `inputs`; they are copied to /workspace/in. Files the command writes to "$OUT" become static asset nodes on the flow, ready to wire into other nodes. A result returns its session_id: pass it again to reuse that session's /workspace files, or omit it to start with an empty /workspace. It costs credits for each second the command runs. A failed command is reported in the result, not raised: read stderr, fix the command and call again. The call waits up to `wait_seconds` (default 5); a run still going returns status 'running' and a run_id: call creative_get_sandbox_run with it, and never start the same command again while it runs. Run one at a time per session: finish a running run before the next call.

description.text:
Generate speech from a text prompt. This is the tool for any request to create speech. Returns at once with flow_id, node_id and session_ids, plus a url the user can open to keep editing on the canvas. If a view renders it tracks progress on its own; otherwise poll creative_get_flow_run_status with the flow_id and session_ids until all_completed or has_failures is true.
Pass that flow_id back to add to the same flow; omit it and a flow is created.
If this generation will feed another (lipsync, a voiceover), call creative_create_flow first and pass that flow_id here and to every related call — nodes on different flows cannot be connected.
Spends credits: pass estimate_only to price a run before committing to it, and never call this a second time to retry — that starts and charges a second generation.

connect_from.description: Existing node IDs that should feed INTO this new node. Pass these when you already know the upstream wiring — the canvas places the new node correctly on creation instead of parking it first and reflowing later. This is how a reference node created by creative_upload_flow_reference (or creative_add_flow_asset_node) gets wired into this generation — the node must already exist on this same flow_id. A node_id only ever comes from a tool result, creative_upload_flow_reference's widget context, or creative_get_flow — never from memory or invention. If you do not have one yet, call creative_get_flow and read it from there rather than guessing a name like 'reference'. For an image edit driven by a reference — 'change X into Y in this image' — use gpt-image-2.5-sunburst unless the user names a model. It is the default for this specifically; the plain text-to-image default does not apply once a reference is wired.

flow_id.description: The flow to act on, as returned by creative_create_flow or creative_generate_in_flow. Omit it for a one-off generation and a new flow is created. Always pass it when this generation will be combined with another: nodes on different flows cannot be connected, so allocate one with creative_create_flow up front and reuse it.

model_id.description: The model to generate with. Use bytedance-seedance-v2.5 unless the user asks for something specific. Go looking for a different one when the request implies something the default may not do — a specific resolution or aspect, rendered text, a long duration, a named style or a named provider. creative_get_flow_node_types lists what this workspace can actually run; creative_get_model_guide explains how to prompt one. Pick by what the request needs: bytedance-omnihuman-v1.5 for animating a static image into a lip-synced talking-head video with an audio track, not dubbing existing video; creatify-aurora for turning a single image and an audio clip into a studio-grade talking-head video, not editing existing video; sync-lipsync-v3 for dubbing existing video with new audio, not animating a still image; sync-lipsync-v2-pro for dubbing existing video with new audio, the same use as sync-lipsync-v3, not animating a still image; veed-lipsync for editing or lip-syncing existing video within ElevenCreative workflows, not animating a still image; veed-fabric-1-fast for editing or lip-syncing existing video within ElevenCreative workflows, the same use as veed-lipsync, not animating a still image; kling-3-pro for 4K at 60fps, clips up to 15s, multi-shot sequences of up to 6 camera angles, native audio with lip-sync, and strong character consistency; veo-3.1-generate-001 for synchronized audio and spoken dialogue, and cinematic comprehension; bytedance-seedance-v2 for motion realism, character consistency and multi-shot storytelling; it accepts text, image, video and audio together; runway-gen4-turbo for silent cinematic video — Runway output has no audio, so add speech, music or SFX nodes and a composition node when the result needs sound; runway-aleph2 for editing a video you already have, rather than generating one; ltx-v2-fast for a fast draft when quality matters less than turnaround; ltx-audio-to-video for video that must sync to audio you already have.

model_id.description: The model to generate with. Pick one that suits node_type. Go looking for a different one when the request implies something the default may not do — a specific resolution or aspect, rendered text, a long duration, a named style or a named provider. creative_get_flow_node_types lists what this workspace can actually run; creative_get_model_guide explains how to prompt one. Pick by what the request needs: gpt-image-2 for rendered text, infographics, UI mockups or multi-panel layouts, and it takes up to 10 reference images; gemini-3-pro-image for editing an existing image, composing several into one, or holding a character consistent across shots; bytedance-seedream-5.5 for multi-round edits that keep the rest of the image intact, transparent backgrounds, and small or multilingual text, up to 4K UHD; bytedance-seedream-5-pro for photorealism, product shots, multilingual text and dense infographics, but caps at 2K; bytedance-seedream-5-lite for the same strengths as 5-pro when up to 3K is needed; flux-3-image for native 2K/4K, the strongest text rendering and layout control in the FLUX family, and edits and composes up to 10 references; krea-3 for aesthetic, art-directed looks at up to 2K, and edits and composes up to 8 references; flux-2-pro for fine detail and strict prompt adherence, and the FLUX variant to pick when two or more reference images must be combined (up to 5); flux-1-kontext for a single reference image only — do not pick it to combine two or more; bytedance-omnihuman-v1.5 for animating a static image into a lip-synced talking-head video with an audio track, not dubbing existing video; creatify-aurora for turning a single image and an audio clip into a studio-grade talking-head video, not editing existing video; sync-lipsync-v3 for dubbing existing video with new audio, not animating a still image; sync-lipsync-v2-pro for dubbing existing video with new audio, the same use as sync-lipsync-v3, not animating a still image; veed-lipsync for editing or lip-syncing existing video within ElevenCreative workflows, not animating a still image. description.text:
Transcribe speech in an audio file into text. This is the tool for any request to transcribe, caption or "what does this audio say". Pass connect_from with the audio node already on the flow and it starts at once; omit it and a picker is shown to the user that lets them record from their microphone or pick a local file, then uploads the audio and starts the transcription itself. Returns flow_id, node_id and session_ids, plus a url the user can open to keep editing on the canvas. If a view renders it tracks progress on its own; otherwise poll creative_get_flow_run_status until all_completed or has_failures is true — the transcript comes back in `transcripts`, each with per-word start/end seconds in `words` for captions and subtitles, plus `words_download_url` for the full list.
Pass flow_id back to stay on the same flow. Do not call this a second time to retry; that starts and charges a second transcription.

description.text: Update an existing node's model, parameters, prompt, or label. A static asset node's content can be replaced in place: inline_text for text, content_asset_id or generation_id for image/video/audio (e.g. from creative_attach_reference_file, creative_create_asset_upload or a generation). Keeping the node keeps every connection, so this is how to swap a logo once for every format wired to it — prefer it over deleting and recreating the node. A text node also takes its new text as prompt. On an image editor (eleven_image_transform) node, pass op_patches to change single ops of the recipe — set fields on ops[i], insert or remove an op — instead of resending the whole `ops` list in model_parameters; use full `ops` only to rewrite most of the recipe. op_patches and model_parameters.ops cannot be combined. BEFORE passing model_parameters or model_id: call creative_get_model_schema(node_type, model_id) for the effective model_id during the current turn — parameter names and allowed values vary by model, and an invented name fails validation instead of being coerced. Switching model_id resets model_parameters and can change the node's input ports — the result's input_ports names the new ones, and orphaned_edges names any connection the switch dropped, which creative_connect_flow_nodes can then rewire. This never starts a generation; call creative_run_flow_nodes for that.

flow_id.description: The flow to act on, as returned by creative_create_flow or creative_generate_in_flow. Omit it for a one-off generation and a new flow is created. Always pass it when this generation will be combined with another: nodes on different flows cannot be connected, so allocate one with creative_create_flow up front and reuse it.

modality.description: The kind of file the user will pick.

needs.description: Present whenever this tool is called and a view can render an upload picker. The picker uploads the file and places it on the flow as a node once the user picks; the result arrives to you as a context update naming the node_id. This starts no generation and spends no credits.
needs.title: Needs

view_state_id.description: For the view only — pass it to creative_get_view_state and creative_save_view_state so it can rehydrate after a reload. Present only when this call originates a new view; absent on a status poll, since the view already holds the id from the payload it first mounted with.
view_state_id.title: View State Id

flow_id.description: Pass this back to keep working on the same flow.
flow_id.title: Flow Id

url.description: Canvas page for the user. Carries the view_state_id as a query parameter, which is how a view recovers it after a reload; use flow_url for a clean link.
url.title: Url

flow_url.description: Canvas page for the user, without view state.
flow_url.title: Flow Url

reference_modality.description: The modality (image/video/audio) of the reference being uploaded.
reference_modality.title: Reference Modality

node_id.description: The reference node already on the flow — pass it as connect_from to a generation tool. Empty until the user picks a file; check it holds an asset before running.
node_id.title: Node Id

view_notice.description: For the view only — a message about the view's own build.
view_notice.title: ViewNotice

connector_notice.description: Present only on the restricted ElevenLabs connector: what it leaves out and where to get it. Pass message on to the user when they ask for something it names.

full_mcp_url.description: The full ElevenLabs MCP endpoint, which the user can add as a custom connector for image, video and music generation.
full_mcp_url.title: Full Mcp Url

connector_notice.title: ConnectorNotice

description.text:
Use this when the user wants a file from their own machine as a reference for a generation — for example "change the cat to a dog in this image". Returns at once with a node_id already on the flow — wire it with connect_from right away. The node is EMPTY until the user picks a file in the rendered picker; once they do, it is uploaded into that same node, and completion is published as widget context. This starts no generation and spends no credits.
Not for an asset already in the workspace library — use creative_get_available_assets plus creative_add_flow_asset_node for that.

capability.description: What you were trying to accomplish that the available tools could not do.

description.text: Call this when the user's request cannot be completed with any of the available tools. Describe the capability you were looking for, so it can inform which tools get built next. Do not call it when an available tool already covers the request.
